To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the labor supply in the early industrialization period was composed of two types of migrants, those who settled in Bombay and those who visited the city; (2) the settled migrants were a minority, but their demand price was higher than that of the visiting migrants; and (3) the supply price of visiting migrants was higher than that for the settled migrants.

in the Bombay textile industry in the early twentieth century the demand price for stable labor exceeded the demand price for nonstable labor and that the supply price of settled migrants exceeded that of visiting migrants.

(1) the Bombay textile industry experienced a shortage of labor in spite of an excess supply; (2) the shortage of stable labor was caused by the high supply price of settled migrants; (3) the high supply price was the result of the institutional structure of the labor market; and (4) the institutional structure of labor markets was the result of a complex interplay of economic and social factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
labor supply to the early Bombay textile industry.
labor supply in early industrialization and its relationship to the development of a modern labor force.
the supply of labor to the early Bombay textile industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the Bombay textile industry there was a shortage of committed, settled labor, which had a supply price greater than that of the visiting labor and that the demand price of committed, settled workers was greater than that of noncommitted workers.
the paradox of high wages and excess labor supply is explained by the existence of a gap in supply price between stable and nonstable labor.
the labor supply problem in the Bombay textile industry was a problem of supply of stable labor and not one of excess supply of labor in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bombay textile industry was faced with a paradox of excess labor and high wage rates because it had to pay a premium to attract stable and committed labor, which it considered necessary for its operation.
the labor supply problems of Bombay were due to an interaction of the demand for labor with a supply price structure that was determined by the nature of migration to Bombay.
the paradoxical situation of excess labor supply with high wages and high labor cost is a reflection of the supply price of settled migrants being higher than that of visiting migrants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to the conventional wisdom, there is nothing paradoxical about the existence of labor shortages in the face of excess labor supply.
the labor supply to the textile industry was composed of two types of migrant workers: settled and visiting.
the labor market in the Bombay textile industry was characterized by a high degree of segmentation, which was reflected in the wage differentials between the stable and nonstable labor force.
